transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what made me come in is that my eating has gotten all turned around lately. Some days I just forget lunch completely. It just completely slips my mind. 

Which is funny, because I used to be the one making lunch for everybody, you know? Back when the kids were little, it was always sandwiches and soup at noon sharp. My youngest, Tommy, he would only eat tomato soup if I put exactly five saltines in it. He's an accountant now, out in Chicago. It's so windy there... I always worry about him driving in the snow. He just bought a new truck though, a big red one, so maybe that helps with the ice. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, my meals. Yeah, so if I'm not forgetting to eat, other days I just find myself standing at the kitchen counter eating crackers and sweets. Just standing there chewing on them, even though nothing really tastes right to me anymore.
When did you first start noticing that you were having trouble remembering to eat or losing your train of thought?

Well, let me think... I'd say this whole change has been going on for about a year and five months. That was right around the time my sister’s health took that serious turn. She had to go into the hospital over in Springfield, and you know, the parking there is just terrible. You have to park in this huge concrete garage and walk across that glass bridge to get to the main building. I always hated that bridge, it makes you feel like you're just floating in the air over the traffic. 

My sister, she used to love heights, though. When we were girls, she’d climb right to the top of the old oak tree in our backyard... well, until lightning struck it back in '82. We had to get the stump ground down and everything. The man who did it charged an arm and a leg, I remember. I told my husband we should have just left it as a planter for petunias, because petunias are so hardy in the summer... but, oh, I'm sorry, what were you asking me again?
Have you ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure, heart disease, or have you ever had a stroke?

No, no, nothing like that. My heart has always been strong, and my blood pressure is usually right where it should be. They always tell me it's good when they put that cuff on my arm at the clinic. Though I will say, that cuff always pinches me right on the inside of my elbow, and I bruise so easily these days. 

My mother was the exact same way, she’d bruise if you just looked at her wrong. But she lived to be 94, bless her heart. Never had a stroke or anything either. She just loved her garden... she grew the biggest tomatoes you ever saw. Beefsteaks, she called them. We’d slice them thick and put them on white bread with just a little mayonnaise and salt. You just can't buy tomatoes that taste like that at the supermarket anymore, they're always so mealy and pale. I tried growing some on my back patio last summer, but the squirrels got to every single one of them before they even turned red. Those squirrels are so bold nowadays, they'll come right up to the screen door and just stare at you... 

Um, I'm sorry, did you ask me something else about my heart?
Are you still able to manage your own finances, such as paying your monthly bills or balancing your checkbook, without any help?

Well, the bills... yes, I suppose I still pay them, though I definitely need more reminders now. I used to be so careful with all of that. I used to handle all the family tasks, making sure everyone was where they needed to be. I even taught craft classes at the community center. Oh, those classes were so much fun. We made the most beautiful wreaths last autumn, with real dried leaves and little acorns that we painted gold. 

I bought this special gold paint from the craft store downtown—the one next to the old bakery. That bakery used to make the best eclairs, but they closed down a few years ago. The owner, Mr. Henderson, he retired and moved to Florida. I think a lot of people move to Florida when they retire, but I could never stand the humidity. My hair just frizzes right up the second I step outside. It’s like a poodle, I swear. I tried this new shampoo they had on sale at the pharmacy, but it smelled too much like coconut. I never liked coconut, not even in macaroons... 

Wait, what was I saying about the bills? Oh, right. I still manage to stay in my home, but I just put off things that used to be routine. I've missed some calls and appointments lately, too. It just feels harder to keep track of it all.
Have you or your family noticed any recent changes in your personality, or have you been acting in ways that seem impulsive or socially inappropriate compared to how you used to be?

No, I wouldn't say that. I haven't been acting out or doing anything inappropriate. I mean, my daughter comes by sometimes and she hasn't said anything about me acting strange, just that I seem a little down. She brought over this casserole last week... chicken and wild rice, I think. She always uses that cream of mushroom soup in the can. 

I remember when soup used to come in those cans that you had to open with the key, you know? You'd twist it and twist it, and the metal would curl up around the key. You had to be so careful not to cut your finger on the edge. My brother cut his thumb wide open on a coffee can once. Bled all over my mother's good linoleum floor. She had just waxed it, too. She used to get down on her hands and knees with the paste wax... it smelled like turpentine and lemons. They don't make floors like that anymore, everything is that fake wood stuff that clicks together. 

Anyway... no, I haven't been acting impulsive or anything like that. Just... tired, mostly.
Have you noticed any stiffness in your muscles, tremors, or any changes in how you walk or keep your balance lately?

No, I don't think so. No shaking or stiffness. I still get around okay, though I always make sure to wear my good walking shoes if I'm going out. I bought them at that shoe store over at the mall—the one where they still measure your foot with that cold metal sliding thing. 

My husband used to swear by a good, sturdy shoe. He wore those heavy leather wingtips to work every single day. He’d sit out on the back step on Sunday mornings with a little tin of black polish and an old cotton rag... usually one of his undershirts that had gotten too thin at the elbows. Waste not, want not, that’s what we were always taught. People just throw everything straight in the trash now. I saw a perfectly good wooden chair sitting out on the curb just down the street from me on Tuesday. It just needed a little sanding and maybe some fresh varnish. My father used to do woodwork in our garage when I was a little girl... he made this beautiful cedar chest for my sister when she got married. It smelled so wonderful when you opened it, just like a pine forest... 

I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Did you ask me about my walking? No, my balance is fine, I haven't noticed any trouble with that.
